title: PROMAX 350 vs PROMAX 500: which welding helmet?
content:
Where the two helmets differ

The PROMAX 350 and PROMAX 500 share a lot: 4 arc sensors, dual shade range 5-8 / 9-13, grind mode, adjustable delay and sensitivity, hinge and lock cover lens retainer, magnification lens holder and full-laminate lens construction. Both suit MIG, stick, TIG, grinding, plasma cutting and air-arc gouging.

Viewing area. The 350 has a 100 x 53mm window, which Weldclass rates larger than many helmets in its class. The 500 is close to the same width at 98mm but 87mm tall, an 85cm2 view. Reviewers on the 500 keep coming back to the visibility.

TIG and optics. The 350 is rated for TIG down to 30 amps. The 500 is rated down to 5 amps and has 1/1/1/1 rated optics, so it is the better pick for low-amp TIG.

Running costs. The two use different batteries (CR2032 for the 350, CR2450 for the 500) and different cover lens part numbers, so check spares before you buy a second helmet.

Both carry a 2-year standard warranty, with 7 years on the auto-darkening lens when you register online within 30 days of purchase.

Both suit MIG, stick, TIG, grinding, plasma cutting and air-arc gouging. Viewing area. […]

meta.verdict: Pick the PROMAX 350 Welding Helmet for MIG, stick and general TIG work at a lower RRP of $158. Pick the PROMAX 500 Welding Helmet if you TIG weld below 30 amps or want a much taller 98 x 87mm view with 1/1/1/1 rated optics, for $199.

faq.q: Is the PROMAX 350 or PROMAX 500 better for TIG welding?
faq.a: The PROMAX 500 Welding Helmet is rated for TIG welding down to 5 amps and has 1/1/1/1 rated optics. The PROMAX 350 Welding Helmet is rated for TIG down to 30 amps. For low-amp TIG work, the PROMAX 500 is the better choice.

faq.q: How much bigger is the PROMAX 500 viewing area?
faq.a: The PROMAX 500 Welding Helmet has a 98 x 87mm (85cm2) viewing area. The PROMAX 350 Welding Helmet has a 100 x 53mm viewing area. The width is similar, but the PROMAX 500 window is 34mm taller.

faq.q: What batteries do the PROMAX 350 and PROMAX 500 use?
faq.a: The PROMAX 350 Welding Helmet uses a replaceable CR2032 battery and the PROMAX 500 Welding Helmet uses a replaceable CR2450 battery. Both also have solar assist. Weldclass does not supply the batteries, which are available from battery retailers and wholesalers.

title: FORCE 180MST vs FURY 165 MPST Pulse: which welder?
content:
Where the two machines differ

Both are 10A MIG/Stick/TIG welders that take 1kg and 5kg spools and accept a spool gun. The differences are in output, controls and what comes in the box.

Output and thickness. The FORCE 180MST delivers 180A @ 10% duty cycle and MIG welds mild steel up to 8mm. The FURY 165 MPST Pulse delivers 165A @ 14% and MIG welds mild steel up to 6mm. On stainless and aluminium the FURY is rated up to 8mm, and its stick capacity is also up to 8mm.

Pulse and synergic control. The FURY offers pulse mode in MIG, Stick and TIG, which Weldclass rates for very low spatter and low distortion on aluminium, stainless and carbon steel. It also has synergic MIG, where you set wire type and size and adjust one dial for thickness. The 180MST is a manual machine with digital readouts and a settings guide inside the door, which several reviewers mention.

In the box. The 180MST standard package includes a heavy-duty 3m BZL 25 torch, gas regulator and hose, 3m leads and drive rollers for gas and gasless wire. The FURY Value Kit adds a PROMAX 130 auto-darkening helmet, gloves, MIG pliers and a cooler bag.

Both carry a 7-year warranty offer that requires online registration within 30 days of purchase. Find a stockist at Where to buy.

faq.q: Which welds thicker steel, the FORCE 180MST or the FURY 165 MPST Pulse?
faq.a: The FORCE 180MST MIG/Stick/TIG Welder MIG welds mild steel up to 8mm at 180A @ 10% duty cycle. The FURY 165 MPST Pulse MIG/Stick/TIG Welder MIG welds mild steel up to 6mm at 165A @ 14%, though it is rated up to 8mm on stainless, aluminium and with stick electrodes.

faq.q: Which is better for welding aluminium?
faq.a: Both machines are spool gun ready. The FURY 165 MPST Pulse adds pulse MIG, rated for aluminium from 1.2mm to 8mm with 1.0mm wire, and a geared 2-roll drive suited to soft aluminium wire. The FORCE 180MST has no pulse function. The FURY 165 is not suitable for TIG welding aluminium, which needs AC/DC TIG.

faq.q: Do both machines run on a 10A power point?
faq.a: Yes. The FORCE 180MST MIG/Stick/TIG Welder is fitted with a 10A 240V plug and the FURY 165 MPST Pulse MIG/Stick/TIG Welder is fitted with a 10A 230V plug for a 230-240V supply. On a generator the 180MST needs at least 8kVA and the FURY 165 at least 7kVA.

title: FORCE 180MST vs FORCE 200MST: which welder?
content:
Where the two machines differ

The FORCE 180MST and FORCE 200MST share the same three processes (gas and gasless MIG, stick and lift-arc TIG), digital readouts, a heavy-duty BZL 25 torch and spool gun capability. The choice mostly comes down to your power supply and how long you weld at a stretch.

Power supply. The 180MST is fitted with a 10A plug, so it runs from a standard outlet. The 200MST is fitted with a 15A plug. Both need a generator of at least 8kVA, with 10kVA ideal.

Duty cycle and capacity. The 200MST is rated at 200A @ 25% duty cycle against 180A @ 10% for the 180MST, so it runs far longer at high output. It also MIG welds mild steel up to 10mm, against 8mm for the 180MST, and adds inductance control for fine-tuning the arc.

Size and wire. The 180MST weighs 9kg and takes 1kg or 5kg spools, which suits carrying around and small jobs. The 200MST weighs 13kg and takes 5kg or 15kg spools, so you change wire less often on bigger jobs. It also comes with 4m leads and torch against 3m on the 180MST.

Both carry a 2-year standard warranty, extended to 7 years when you register online within 30 days of purchase.

faq.q: Can the FORCE 200MST plug into a 10A power point?
faq.a: The FORCE 200MST MIG/Stick/TIG Welder is fitted with a 15A 240V plug. If you only have a standard 10A outlet, the FORCE 180MST MIG/Stick/TIG Welder is the model in this pair fitted with a 10A 240V plug.

faq.q: Which has the higher duty cycle, the FORCE 180MST or FORCE 200MST?
faq.a: The FORCE 200MST MIG/Stick/TIG Welder is rated at 200A @ 25% duty cycle. The FORCE 180MST MIG/Stick/TIG Welder is rated at 180A @ 10%. For longer runs at high output, the 200MST is the stronger choice.

The FORCE 200MST MIG/Stick/TIG Welder takes 5kg (D200mm) or 15kg (D300mm) spools. The FORCE 180MST MIG/Stick/TIG Welder takes 1kg (D100mm) or 5kg (D200mm) spools, which suits smaller jobs and a lighter 9kg machine.

title: FORCE 135ST vs FORCE 180ST: which stick welder?
content:
Where the two machines differ

The FORCE 135ST and FORCE 180ST are both stick welders with DC lift-arc TIG, adjustable hot start and arc force, and an optional VRD. Neither includes a TIG torch or regulator, which are optional extras for both.

Power and electrodes. The 135ST is fitted with a 10A plug and runs electrodes up to 3.2mm, with 140A @ 20% duty cycle and a 77V open circuit voltage for easy striking. The 180ST needs a 15A outlet and steps up to 180A @ 18% and electrodes up to 4.0mm.

Portability. At 2.3kg and 250 x 95 x 140mm, the 135ST is about half the weight of the 4.5kg 180ST. Reviewers on the 135ST mostly comment on how light and compact it is for the output.

Leads and extras. The 180ST comes with 4m earth and stick leads, a 3m power lead and an LCD meter. The 135ST has 3m leads and includes welding gloves.

On a generator, the 135ST needs at least 7kVA and the 180ST at least 8kVA. Both carry a 2-year standard warranty, extended to 7 years when you register online within 30 days of purchase.

faq.q: Can the FORCE 135ST run 3.2mm electrodes on 10A power?
faq.a: Yes. The FORCE 135ST Stick/TIG Welder is fitted with a 10A 240V plug and is rated for electrodes up to 3.2mm, with 140A @ 20% duty cycle. For 4.0mm electrodes, the FORCE 180ST Stick/TIG Welder is rated up to 4.0mm but needs a 15A outlet.

faq.q: Can the FORCE 135ST or FORCE 180ST TIG weld aluminium?
faq.a: No. The FORCE 135ST and FORCE 180ST Stick/TIG Welders do DC lift-arc TIG only, suited to steel and stainless. TIG welding aluminium needs AC/DC capability, such as the FORCE 201T AC/DC Pulse TIG Welder.

faq.q: What size generator do the FORCE 135ST and FORCE 180ST need?
faq.a: The FORCE 135ST Stick/TIG Welder needs a generator of at least 7kVA, with 8kVA ideal. The FORCE 180ST Stick/TIG Welder needs at least 8kVA, with 10kVA or more ideal. The FORCE 180ST also comes with a long 3m power input lead for site use.
